questions.q: Why can't real quantum hardware ever give you a `Statevector`-style exact amplitude readout directly?
options: Real hardware doesn't support the Hadamard gate
You cannot read out a qubit's amplitude by observing it, only by measuring it, which collapses it to a classical bit
Statevector simulation is only a theoretical concept with no real meaning
Real hardware always has more than 2 qubits, making it incompatible
questions.explain: Measurement collapses a qubit to a classical outcome; physics doesn't allow reading an amplitude directly, which is exactly why exact statevector access only exists in simulation.

questions.q: For the Bell-state circuit `qc.h(0); qc.cx(0,1)` with no measurement, what does `Statevector(qc)` give for the amplitude on `01`?
options: It cannot be computed without measurement
questions.explain: The exact statevector has amplitude 0 on both `01` and `10` — those outcomes are impossible for this entangled state, with no sampling error involved since nothing was sampled.

questions.q: A noiseless shot-based run of the same circuit at shots=4096 gave `{'00': 2021, '11': 2075}` instead of exactly 2048/2048. What is the source of this gap?
options: Depolarizing gate error in the simulator
Statistical sampling noise from drawing a finite number of shots
questions.explain: The simulator here models zero hardware error. The only possible source of the observed deviation from the exact 0.5/0.5 split is sampling noise inherent to drawing a finite number of shots.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts statevector simulation and shot-based simulation?
options: They always produce identical numeric outputs
Statevector simulation gives exact ground-truth probabilities with no sampling; shot-based simulation only ever gives a noisy estimate of those probabilities, even when noiseless
Shot-based simulation is always more accurate because it uses real measurement
Statevector simulation requires measurement gates, shot-based simulation does not
questions.explain: Statevector simulation computes the exact amplitudes with zero sampling. Shot-based simulation, even with a perfectly noiseless simulator, only ever estimates those probabilities from a finite number of sampled outcomes.

questions.q: Which API call retrieves an exact statevector in Qiskit, and what must be true of the circuit passed to it?
options: `Statevector(qc)`; the circuit must contain no measurement gates
`qc.get_counts()`; the circuit must be transpiled first
questions.explain: `qiskit.quantum_info.Statevector(qc)` computes the exact amplitude vector directly, but only works correctly when the circuit has no measurement operations collapsing the state.
